subject: E2E latency stability & streaming SLOs — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Joanne Park <joanne.park@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: demo recap + targets

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — that was helpful. Quick recap from our side and a handful of asks so we can decide next steps: 

- Goal: move NLP inference for triage & routing to a hosted provider. Primary concerns are p95/p99 E2E latency under production mixes (concurrent API calls + streaming responses for live transcript enrichment).
- Current provider: average p95 ~220ms (end-to-end with our ingress + model) but p99 spikes to 1.8s under bursty traffic; streaming sessions often see tail jitter when concurrency crosses ~40 streams.

As discussed, we need:
1) Clear baseline: p95 target <= 250ms, p99 <= 1.2s (we're flexible on p99 if mitigations shown).
2) Throughput booking: steady-state 350 QPS with short bursts to 800 QPS for 3–5 minutes.
3) Streaming: support 100 concurrent streaming sessions with <=75ms per-chunk overhead and graceful degradation (fallback to poll) when overloaded.

Attached a lightweight traffic matrix (nimble_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx) with our request distribution. Can you confirm Redwood's ability to reach the targets on hosted with a clear validation plan?

Next steps we'd like: one small spike test (10–15 minutes), then a 24-hour soak with our traffic mix. Proposed window: Oct 26–27.

Thanks,
Liam
Director, Platform Engineering
NimbleHealth

---
Attachment: nimble_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo recap + targets

Liam — really valuable session, thanks. Short answers up front, then a proposed validation plan.

- Baseline: Hosted Redwood API can meet p95 <= 250ms for your mix in our initial profiling; p99 depends on burst shaping and KV cache effectiveness but we have documented mitigations to target <=1.2s.
- Throughput: we can provision a Dedicated-capacity plan for steady 350 QPS and allow bursts to 800 QPS with autoscaling + transient capacity buffers.
- Streaming: our streaming stack supports the per-chunk overhead you listed (typically 40–80ms under standard gen/stream kernels). For sustained concurrent sessions we recommend prefix caching and a per-tenant concurrency cap with graceful fallback to polling when needed.

Proposed validation plan (high level):
1) Profile run (2–4 hours): Redwood runs your attached traffic matrix against a hosted test model variant to collect realistic latency envelopes. We'll share token-level breakdowns (ingress, model, network).
2) Spike test (10–15m): replicate your burst window (800 QPS) to observe tail behavior & autoscaler reaction.
3) Streaming concurrency ramp (1h): ramp streaming sessions from 10 -> 100 concurrent streams, monitor per-chunk overhead and per-session tail.
4) 24-hour soak: your traffic mix with scheduled synthetic bursts.

We'll provide an SLO acceptance checklist and a named runbook if you'd like Redwood engineers on standby during the soak. Attached is our SLO playbook (rdw_slo_playbook_v2.pdf) for your review.

Can Marissa lead the technical runbook and the scheduling? If Oct 26–27 is still good, we'll provision test endpoints and a HubSpot run record (linked).

Thanks — I'll loop Marissa and Ben to align on instrumentation and tracing hooks.

— Sergio
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications and the test checklist we'll follow. Quoting Sergio above for context.

On Sun, 18 Oct 2026 at 17:08, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed validation plan (high level):
> 1) Profile run (2–4 hours): Redwood runs your attached traffic matrix against a hosted test model variant to collect realistic latency envelopes.

Notes / checklist for engineering:
- Model variant: we'll use q4f16 quantized variant for initial profiling (matches your accuracy window). We'll include a non-quantized run to check regression margins.
- Instrumentation: please add X-Request-Id header to each call and share a short-lived log sink we can write to (S3 or GCS). Traces at the token level are ideal but we can work with coarse buckets if necessary.
- Network: ask your infra team to run the spike test from the same region (us-west-2) and avoid WAN proxies between test clients and our hosted endpoint.
- Streaming specifics: we'll measure per-chunk latency + cumulative session tail. If we observe jitter above 120ms per chunk at any point during concurrency ramp, we'll enable adaptive chunk sizing fallback.
- Acceptance criteria (pass/fail): p95 <= 250ms across the 24h run; p99 <=1.2s for 95% of test windows (5-minute windows), and streaming per-chunk <= 75ms median; fallback behavior validated for graceful degradation.

Deliverables we'll provide before the window:
- Test endpoints + credentials (expires after test)
- Runbook with roles & contact matrix
- Live dashboard (token-level cost/latency breakdowns)

Can you confirm NimbleHealth can provide the log sink and a short-lived API key for the planned window? If so, we'll create the HubSpot run and book the Redwood on-call shift.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear checklist. Confirming:
- We can stand up an S3 sink with a short-lived bucket and create an API key for the test endpoints (can you provide expected header format for the X-Request-Id?).
- Oct 26–27 window looks OK from our side — I'll loop in infra to ensure tests originate from us-west-2.
- Agree on acceptance criteria; one ask: can Redwood also include a short summary report (CSV of p95/p99 per 5m window + notes on any failovers) within 24 hours of the soak? That will help my CTO and procurement.

If that's fine, consider this confirmed and go ahead with the HubSpot run and booking.

Thanks,
Liam
